"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
With just three days until Election Day, many states are still registering eligible voters for the midterms.
As NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports, today's the last chance to register in North Carolina.
The window is closing today for eligible voters in North Carolina to sign up in person at the state's early voting sites.
They're set to close at 3 p.m. Eastern.
The only state where voter registration is not required is North Dakota.
And many states allow for same-day registration at the polls on Tuesday's Election Day.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend going to your state's official election website
to confirm your status and contact information before casting your ballot.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their name, or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
This midterm season, some surprisingly close races are unfolding in once solidly Republican red states.
As Rick Thorrington of Member Station WRKF reports, Louisiana has joined their ranks.
Democrat Jamie Davis, a black third-generation farmer, is running for Senate against Republican Congresswoman Julia Letlow.
LSU political science professor Robert Hogan sees significance in President Trump's announcement this week.
That he'll appear in a virtual rally for Letlow on Monday.
It seems to demonstrate that Jamie Davis is doing quite well in a state where Donald Trump won with about 60 percent of the vote in the last presidential election.
So this has to be very encouraging for the Democrats.
Many pundits thought it would be a cakewalk for Letlow, but the Davis grassroots campaign is giving her a run for her money.
Davis is the first black nominee for Senate in Louisiana since Reconstruction.
For NPR News, I'm Brooke Thorrington and Baton Rouge.
A grand jury in Texas has indicted an ICE officer accused of intentionally hitting a Mexican construction worker with his car earlier this month.
The man was later placed in custody with a broken leg.
Houston Public Media's Bianca Seward has more.
Mario Alberto Morales was indicted for a second-degree felony offense of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
Harris County District Attorney Sean Tiers says he hopes the indictment will send a message.
An ICE badge does not give you free rein to injure, kill, or violate the constitutional rights of anyone.
An ICE spokesperson claimed the victim Miguel Parra Hernandez ran in front of the agent's vehicle while they were trying to arrest a different man.
Parra Hernandez's lawyer has disputed ICE's account.
Surveillance video of the incident shows the agent driving towards Parra Hernandez as he runs away from the car and into a parking lot where the collision occurred.
For NPR News, I'm Bianca Seward in Houston.
Daylight saving time ends overnight at 2 a.m. for most of the country.
It's when we set clocks back one hour.
Most people change their clocks before they go to bed.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he's considering apologizing for the U.K.'s role in the transatlantic slave trade.
This is as he tries to strengthen relations with countries in Africa and the Caribbean.
If it happens, it would be a first.
In an opinion piece in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham says Britain needs to acknowledge its "complicated history" to protect the Commonwealth.
And King Charles, who started his first Caribbean tour as king this past week, acknowledged "the great suffering caused by slavery."
Both men head to Antigua on Monday.
The deciding Game 7 of the WNBA Finals tips off tonight between the Golden State, Valkyries, and the Atlanta Dream.
Nina Thorson from member station KQED has a preview.
After her team lost Game 6 on Thursday, Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase said her players hadn't executed very well,
but she was confident they would be ready for Game 7.
The physicality is supposed to be ramped up.
These are win or die. This is do or die. This is it.
Whichever team wins, it'll be a milestone for their franchise.
The Atlanta Dream have been to the Finals three times, most recently in 2013, but they've never won.
The Golden State Valkyries have never been to the Finals, but this is only their second season in existence.
The Valkyries hope to get an edge from an enthusiastic home crowd that's already made them the most valuable franchise in the WNBA.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Thorson.
On Wall Street this week, all three of the major indices ended the week in the red with a doll falling more than a tenths of a percent.
